dissertations.title: The Egyptian Navy after Muhammad Ali Pasha, 1848-1898
dissertations.summary: A study of how a secondary navy projected power across the Black Sea, Mediterranean and Indian Ocean despite its limited size, and of its role in Egyptian political, territorial and military strategy.
dissertations.imageAlt: First page of The Egyptian Navy after Muhammad Ali Pasha, 1848-1898

dissertations.title: Friend of My Enemy: China, Iran and Their Unshared Adversaries
dissertations.summary: A comparative analysis of China’s relations with Iran and Iran’s regional adversaries, using arms transfers, trade and UN General Assembly voting alignment to assess the depth of Sino-Iranian ties.
dissertations.imageAlt: First page of Friend of My Enemy: China, Iran and Their Unshared Adversaries

essays.title: Defeat in Detail: Re-Evaluating Japanese Stay-Behind Operations in Shanxi
essays.summary: An account of Japanese troops who remained in Shanxi after 1945, examining their organisation, relationship with Yan Xishan and role in the Chinese Civil War through Chinese and Japanese sources.
essays.imageAlt: First page of Defeat in Detail: Re-Evaluating Japanese Stay-Behind Operations in Shanxi

projects.title: History Evals
projects.summary: Evaluating how AI models respond to workplace assignments reconstructed from historical cases of institutional harm.
projects.imageAlt: Historical sources become workplace assignments, followed by evaluation of model responses

projects.title: Steam and Steel
projects.summary: A late-Victorian total-conversion mod for Medieval II: Total War: Kingdoms.

newsletter.title: Newsletter
newsletter.summary: A news app I developed to help readers explore reporting from different perspectives.

newsletter.title: Meerkat
newsletter.summary: The backend pipeline for Newsletter. It collects, translates and analyses articles, then prepares them for publication in the app.
newsletter.description: Scheduled AWS Fargate tasks process the articles. PostgreSQL stores the results, and a Flask API serves the published material.

ironclads.title: Fleets, Trade and State Power
ironclads.summary: A study of naval power as an economic system: ships depend on finance, ports, supply networks, and the institutions that maintain them.
ironclads.description: The material is organised around fleet construction, commercial routes, and the relationship between military commitments and available resources.

ironclads.title: Fleet Records
ironclads.summary: Comparative notes on ships and the societies that built them, arranged as short entries with supporting references.

introduction.title: Shun Kwok
paragraphs: I study how secondary empires historically projected power in global environments dominated by stronger powers. My research brings together qualitative and quantitative methods, as well comparative approaches to East Asia, the Middle East and Beyond.
My current work examines naval modernization in the 19th century - the prevailing trends, and how various states attempted to mobilize asymmetry.
